title: The King Learns Her Name and Realizes He Was Born Only to Destroy

cuts.raw_narration: Inside the palace throne room, Meruem, the green-skinned Chimera Ant King with a striped tail, sits alone at the wooden Gungi board after Komugi, the blind girl with white spiral pigtails, has asked for a short break. As she starts walking away down the long red carpet, tapping her cane, he stops her. Still facing the board, he calls back over his shoulder and asks her name. Komugi pauses, turns, and answers softly: 'Komugi.' Meruem repeats the word to himself, his large purple eyes narrowing in an extreme close-up as if the sound of a name he did not need is settling into him. Komugi, emboldened, bows slightly and asks him in return what his own name is. Meruem's eyes widen. The question hangs in silence. He does not answer. Instead, a wide high-angle shot shows him small at the board and Komugi tiny in the far doorway; then the camera cuts outside, up to the palace domes at night, where Neferpitou, the cat-eared Royal Guard, is perched on a golden spire. Pitou drops down from the roof and lands kneeling on the terrace where Meruem is now waiting, summoned without a word.

Under the cloudy night sky, the three Royal Guards assemble in front of their King. Neferpitou is joined by Shaiapouf, the blond guard in the dark suit, and Menthuthuyoupi, the huge red-skinned guard, all three kneeling in a row on the palace roof. Meruem points at each of them and confirms who they are — 'Pitou.' 'Poof.' 'Yuppie.' — and each answers 'Yes, Sire.' Then, standing over them with his tail arched behind him, he asks the question the guards have never been asked before: 'So tell me — what is my name?' Pouf's eyes go wide with shock; Pitou looks up, alert; Youpi tenses. Pouf, hand pressed to his chest, stammers out the only answer he has: 'You are the king. You have no other name. You are the one and only king.' He rushes on about imposters who claim the throne and their sacred duty to eliminate them, so that the world will know there is but one true king. Meruem hears him out, arms folded, then answers back with unnerving calm — 'King is merely a title. A title can be bestowed. It is not a name.' The three guards, still kneeling, are silent.

The conversation has turned darker: Meruem has just been confessing that he killed a child on the road for no reason, and Pouf, distraught, is begging him to stop speaking. Meruem cuts him off with two flat words — 'I am king.' — and then falls silent under the full moon. A purple aura begins to bleed off his body. It swells into a roaring column of Nen that lights up the courtyard; Pouf and Youpi flinch back, Pitou stares up in awe. Bathed in that aura, Meruem finishes the thought he had been circling all night. He took a life for no reason at all, he says, so that must mean he possesses tremendous power. He appears without warning to rob countless beings of their inferior strength. The screen cuts to a vast, endless sea of identical brainwashed citizens stretching to the horizon — the crowd whose lives are already his to take. 'To crush. To destroy. Violence is my power, and violence is the ultimate force in the entire world.' Meruem's face fills the screen with a slow, malicious grin, his eyes gleaming through the aura — the King has answered his own question about his name by naming what he was born to do.
